title: Connect the rooks, or something sharper?
outcomes: Checks first whether anything of his is attacked and loose, and whether an enemy piece can be taken
Chooses between a connecting move and a move with a threat or a tempo
Sees when the rooks are already connected and no connecting move is needed

steps.text:
In **Connecting the rooks: a step, not a goal** you saw which pieces stand between the rooks. Here you decide **when**. Ask in this order.
**Is anything of mine attacked and loose? Can I take something loose? Does a developing move also make a threat?**
Connecting the rooks is the answer to none of these; it is what you do when they are all quiet.

steps.caption: Black to move. No Black piece is loose, and the rooks on a8 and h8 do not yet see each other.

line.say: Black castles. The rooks on a8 and f8 now see each other along the back rank.
White plays f4, attacking the pawn on e5.

claims.statement: Before castling the king stands between the rooks.
After O-O the rooks are connected.
Castling is among the engine's first choices.

steps.text:
Connecting comes last on the checklist. **Skip it** when a piece of yours is attacked and loose, when an enemy piece can simply be taken, or when a developing move also makes a threat. Castling may be delayed on purpose.
And when the squares between the rooks are already empty, there is nothing left to connect.
**Rule of thumb:** finish development unless something sharper pays.

steps.title: Same position, one change
steps.prompt: In the first position castling queenside is the move. In the next two, one thing has changed. Predict whether connecting is still the question, then check.
Think of a recent game of yours. At which move did you last connect the rooks, and was a piece of yours attacked or a tempo available at the time?
